interest: This file offers valuable historical insight into Dutch public diplomacy, media campaigns, and political frustration during the Indonesian National Revolution, especially following the controversial Second Police Action (Operatie Kraai) of December 1948 and subsequent United Nations Security Council intervention. It documents how Ons Vrije Nederland, a magazine originating in the anti-Nazi resistance, attempted to reframe international and American perception by portraying Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta not as legitimate democratic independence leaders, but as Axis collaborators and 'Quislings' equivalent to European fascists. The file also reveals the diplomatic balancing act of the Dutch Foreign Ministry, which unofficially distanced itself from personal attacks on leaders with whom it had to negotiate while allowing private media to distribute targeted English-language propaganda to foreign audiences and U.S. lawmakers.
overview: This State Department file contains Foreign Service Despatch No. 104 (March 16, 1949) from Robert Coe, Counselor of Embassy at the American Embassy in The Hague, transmitting to the Secretary of State five copies of the March 5, 1949 issue of the Dutch weekly magazine Ons Vrije Nederland (Our Free Netherlands). The magazine issue, published partly in English and accompanied by an explanatory leaflet, was designed to influence international public opinion—particularly in the United States and within the United Nations Security Council—by highlighting the wartime collaboration of Indonesian Republican leaders Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta with the Japanese military administration. Featuring an 'Open Letter to the members of the Security Council' alongside numerous wartime photographs and quotes, the magazine argues that the Indonesian Republic was an undemocratic Japanese fascist creation and criticizes American and UN support for the republican leadership following the Dutch military action of December 1948. In his cover despatch, Coe notes that Netherlands Foreign Office officials explicitly disavowed the publication as private and unofficial, reiterating the Dutch government's official policy of refraining from personal attacks against individuals with whom it might have to negotiate.

subfiles.from: Robert Coe, Counselor of Embassy, American Embassy, The Hague
subfiles.summary: Robert Coe, Counselor of Embassy at The Hague, transmits to the Secretary of State five copies of the March 5, 1949 issue of the Dutch weekly magazine Ons Vrije Nederland (Our Free Netherlands). The special issue, written partly in English and accompanied by an explanatory leaflet, was prepared specifically to publicize the wartime collaboration of Indonesian leaders Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta with Japan and was aimed at audiences abroad, especially in the United States and the United Nations. Coe notes that when approached by an Embassy officer, the Chief of the Press Section of the Netherlands Foreign Office emphasized that the publication was entirely private and that official Netherlands policy remained committed to avoiding personal attacks on individuals with whom it had to negotiate.

subfiles.about: A special issue of the Dutch weekly Ons Vrije Nederland featuring an Open Letter to the UN Security Council and extensive photographic evidence documenting Sukarno's and Hatta's wartime collaboration with Japan.
subfiles.from: Editorial Staff of Ons Vrije Nederland (Aad van Leeuwen, Editor-in-Chief)
subfiles.summary: This special issue of the former underground resistance weekly Ons Vrije Nederland (O.V.N.) is published partly in English to challenge prevailing American and international sympathy for the Republic of Indonesia. The core of the issue is an 'Open Letter to the members of the Security Council' supported by numerous wartime photographs and quotes documenting Sukarno's and Mohammad Hatta's active collaboration with General Hideki Tojo and Japanese occupation forces, their anti-Allied speeches, and their role in mobilizing Indonesian labor and youth. The editors contend that the Republic of Indonesia was a Japanese military creation and criticize the UN Security Council and U.S. policy for backing these leaders against Dutch federalist plans, while the remainder of the magazine includes a complete Dutch translation of the Open Letter, commercial advertisements, humorous anecdotes, and reader puzzle solutions.
subfiles.title: Special Issue of Ons Vrije Nederland: Open Letter to the Security Council on Sukarno's and Hatta's Collaboration with Japan
subfiles.to: Members of the United Nations Security Council and the General Public
